name: Keenable
summary: Web search and page fetch on Keenable's own index, built for AI agents.

api_key.description: a Keenable API key, starting keen_ (Keenable console > API keys)

notes: Auth is the X-API-Key header. Without a key, Keenable serves keyless /public paths that also need an X-Keenable-Title header; they are rate limited per IP and not in this entry.
402 means the organization is out of credits; do not retry. 429 means wait for Retry-After seconds.
Keenable's docs also describe SELECT (structured web data over SQL) which is not covered here.

endpoints.name: Search the web
endpoints.summary: Semantic search over Keenable's own index; results carry extracted page snippets.

query.description: What to search for; describe the page wanted in plain language.
query.example: blog post comparing React and Vue performance

mode.description: pro (default, deeper) or realtime (fastest); each is billed as its own SKU.

site.description: Only this site; subdomains included, a path narrows further.

published_after.description: Keep pages published at or after this point; pages with no known date are dropped. Takes a date, a timestamp or a relative delta such as 7d.

published_before.description: Keep pages published at or before this point. Takes a date, a timestamp or a relative delta such as 7d.

acquired_after.description: Keep pages indexed at or after this point. Takes a date, a timestamp or a relative delta such as 7d.

acquired_before.description: Keep pages indexed at or before this point. Takes a date, a timestamp or a relative delta such as 7d.

query_time.description: Search the index as it stood at this moment; sets no lower bound.

snippet_max_length.description: Cap on snippet characters per result, 180-10000.

disable_cards.description: Leave out Keenable-written cards; default false.

notes: A read over POST: it runs a search and changes nothing in your account.
published_at is an ISO 8601 string on search results.
Keenable also offers a keyless /v1/search/public path; this entry uses the keyed path.

endpoints.name: Fetch a page as markdown
endpoints.summary: A page's main text as markdown, or only the part a prompt asks for.

url.description: Absolute http or https URL to read.

max_chars.description: Cap on characters of content; default 50000.

live.description: Fetch from the source now instead of the indexed copy; billed as fetch.live.

prompt.description: Up to 2000 characters of instruction; content then holds only the model's answer.

notes: On a fetch response, published_at is Unix seconds, unlike the ISO string on search results.
404 means no page exists at the URL.
